jasper: ran an nsys capture on staging (replica-12) to repro the token-level latency regression. attaching qdrep link: https://internal.profiles/1829504321.qdrep
jasper: quick summary: KV-cache update kernel is now the single largest consumer (≈40% token time). attention kernels keep switching between small-batch and large-batch variants in the middle of the same trace. weird oscillation.
lee: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet or the top kernel table from nsys?
jasper: pasted top of timeline: ```Kernel timeline (aggregated): fused_attn_forward_v2               35.2%
kv_cache_update                      40.1%
cudaMemcpyAsync (host<->dev)         9.8%
small_batch_attn_dispatch            10.4%
other kernels                         4.5%
```
anita: what nsys / cupti / driver combo did you use? this sounds like tooling mis-reporting + runtime choosing the wrong kernel path.
jasper: nsys 2024.1, cupti from CUDA 12.2, driver 535.86. capture run was inside our rootless container (userns + no CAP_SYS_PTRACE).
anita: ok. there are known CUPTI/driver compatibility issues in the 535.x line that make activity records noisy under some container/security setups. nsys 2024.1 also changed how it interacts with CUPTI buffers. recommend two quick checks: (1) repro the capture on host (not container) or with --security-opt seccomp=unconfined; (2) try nsys 2023.4 to see if the timeline behaviour changes. if kernels are mis-attributed the runtime might be seeing wrong latency signals.
ryan: one more angle — our kernel selection heuristic picks between fused_attn (large-batch optimized) and small_batch_attn based on observed batch distribution and an estimated kernel startup cost. if CUPTI misses some short-lived kernels, the estimator can flip-flop mid-run. that would explain the oscillation. we should guard the selector to not flip for <N tokens or within a single request's lifetime.
mika: ops-bot flagged several permission errors when the capture started: "ops-bot: nsys: ERROR: CUPTI: ioctl(CUPTI_IOCTL_RECORD) failed: Permission denied". logs in /var/log/ci-profiles/1829504321.log
jasper: exact stderr from run: ```nsys: Starting capture...
CUPTI ERROR: cuptiActivityEnable: IOCTL failed (errno=13)
Note: some CUPTI activity records may be incomplete.
Profile saved to out.qdrep
```
anita: that IOCTL errno=13 in rootless containers usually means either seccomp blocked the ioctl or the driver refuses access without the right capabilities. two practical workarounds: (A) run profiling on host / privileged container, (B) downgrade to nsys 2023.4 which uses a slightly different CUPTI handshake and is less likely to hit the IOCTL path that fails. both have been effective in our past incidents.
lee: curious — when you downgraded, did the KV-cache dominance change?
jasper: yes. with nsys 2023.4 the kernel timeline is stable: fused_attn stays dominant and kv_cache_update drops to ~18%. when using 2024.1 the capture shows kv_cache_update ~40% and the runtime's observed token times match that regression.
ryan: so two possibilities: (1) 2024.1 + driver combo really changes scheduling/overheads (unlikely but possible), or (2) 2024.1/CUPTI mis-reporting caused our telemetry to steer the runtime into a suboptimal path (i.e., runtime reacted to noisy profiles).
mika: ops-bot followup: we also saw a segfault in nsight host side in two runs. stack snippet: ```nsight: segfault at cuptiActivityFlush -> ioctl -> kernel driver EFAULT``` — filed kernel/driver bug internally against NV driver 535.86.
jasper: immediate mitigations I'm going to try: (1) pin users running profiling to nsys 2023.4 for now; (2) instrument the runtime to detect CUPTI errors (ioctl errno!=0) and disable automatic kernel-selector feedback when toolchain is unreliable; (3) add a safety clamping in selector: no flip within same request, and min consecutive samples before switching.
anita: +1 for safety clamp. also add a debug flag to force kernel path for repro (helps compare perf deterministically): in runtime config add "kernel_selector.forced_path": "fused_attn" or "small_batch_attn".
lee: can you open a small PR to set the default selector hysteresis to 8 consecutive evals? That should be low-impact and quick.
ryan: long term, we should add an in-process micro-trace using cupti activity APIs directly (not relying on external nsys) so the runtime can validate external traces. but that's a bigger project.
jasper: created a short task list in the thread: 1) roll profiling teams to nsys 2023.4 for the next 48h (mika) 2) add CUPTI-error detection + selector-hysteresis (ryan) 3) repro on host to confirm driver bug and escalate to NV partner (anita) 4) add forced_path debug flag (lee)
mika: acked, will message infra and flip default nsys package in the staging image.
ops-bot: deploy job 7739 queued to update staging image (contains nsys 2023.4). ETA ~15m. :gear: :hourglass_flowing_sand:
jasper: thanks folks — will post results after the host-run and after the hysteresis PR lands. if anyone else saw a similar spike in kv cache recently, drop short notes here. :thumbsup:
